channel.title: The Sumba Times
channel.description: News, culture and travel from the island of Sumba, Indonesia

item.title: Bali to Waingapu, non-stop: what the new TransNusa route means for East Sumba
item.description: Since 15 July, East Sumba has a direct link to Bali four times a week. The hard part, says the regent, is keeping it.

item.title: How to get to Sumba from Bali: flights, airports and the route that works best
item.description: Two airports, short flights and one simple rule: arrive at one end of the island and leave from the other.

item.title: The Pasola, explained: Sumba's ritual battle on horseback
item.description: Riders throw blunt wooden spears at each other across an open field. It is not a show. It is a ritual that opens the planting season.

item.title: Marapu, ikat and the traditional villages: a respectful guide to Sumba's culture
item.description: Tall thatched roofs, stone tombs still in use and cloth that takes hundreds of hours to weave.

item.title: Sumba's beaches, lagoons and waterfalls: nine places worth the drive
item.description: From a turquoise lagoon in the north-west to mangroves that seem to dance at sunset in the east.

item.title: Where to stay in Sumba: every kind of hotel on the island, listed fairly
item.description: About 1,500 rooms for an island twice the size of Bali. Here they are, in alphabetical order.

item.title: What is being built on Sumba: the new hotels and projects to watch
item.description: A 127-room hotel in Waingapu, new villas in the west, and no mega-resort on the horizon.

item.title: What people say at the end
item.description: A nurse listened to hundreds of people in their final weeks. They kept saying five things.
